t:
A block of 1 kg is kept on a rough surface of an elevator moving up with constant velocity of 5 m/s. In 10 seconds, the work done by the normal reaction from the ground frame (the block does not slide on the inclined surface): (i) is 320 J (ii) is equal to work done by friction force in elevator frame (iii) is equal to work done by friction in ground frame Of the three statements given above, the ones that are true is given by the choice:
[[img:fd41f1679404]]
s:
Mass of the block m=1 kg.
Velocity of the elevator v=5 m/s (upwards).
Time t=10 s.
Angle of inclination θ=37°.
Displacement of the elevator (and the block, as it doesn’t slide) in the ground frame is:
S=v×t=5×10=50 m (upwards).
The normal reaction N exerted by the inclined surface on the block is perpendicular to the incline.
Since the block is not accelerating with respect to the elevator, and the elevator moves with constant velocity, the net force on the block is zero.
Balancing forces perpendicular to the incline:
N=mgcosθ
N=1×10×cos(37°)=10×4/5=8 N.
The angle between the normal reaction N and the displacement S (which is vertically upwards) is θ=37°.
Work done by the normal reaction from the ground frame is:
W_N=N×S×cos(37°)
W_N=8×50×4/5=8×10×4=320 J.
So, statement (i) is true.
In the elevator frame, the displacement of the block is zero because it does not slide.
Therefore, the work done by friction in the elevator frame is zero.
In the ground frame, the friction force f acts upwards along the incline.
Balancing forces parallel to the incline: f=mgsinθ=1×10×sin(37°)=10×3/5=6 N.
The angle between friction f and vertical displacement S is 90°−37°=53°.
Work done by friction in ground frame: W_f=f×S×cos(53°)=6×50×3/5=180 J.
Since 320 J≠0 and 320 J≠180 J, statements (ii) and (iii) are false.
Only statement (i) is true.
